title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not Grothendieck's manuscript. It is a typed page in English, numbered III.4 and photographed upside down. It appears to come from someone else's thesis or preprint on Azumaya algebras over ringed spaces, and Grothendieck evidently used the back of the sheet as scratch paper. The neighbouring pages, in his hand, are about tori over Q, Hodge structures and effectivity of characters; they have nothing to do with this text.

The typed mathematics works in a ringed space (X, O) with a sheaf of O-algebras L.

Theorem III.2: L is 'locally separable' over O (that is, locally Azumaya) if and only if two conditions hold. First, L is finitely presented as an O-module. Second, each stalk L_x is a central separable (Azumaya) O_x-algebra. It is derived from an earlier Theorem III.1 and a fact on the previous typed page, which we do not have.

Remark: if L is locally separable and M is an L-module that is locally projective of finite type, then M is locally projective of finite type over O.

Lemma III.3: for a commutative ring A and a finitely generated projective A-module M, W = End_A(M) is separable over A.

The proof uses the Auslander–Goldman appendix (presumably reference [5], 'The Brauer group of a commutative ring', 1960, Propositions A.1, A.3 and Theorem A.2):
- The map Hom_A(M,A) ⊗_A M → W, f⊗m ↦ (n ↦ f(n)m), is an isomorphism of W-bimodules, hence a left W^e-isomorphism.
- Hom_A(M,A) is finitely generated projective as a right W-module.
- M is finitely generated projective as a left W-module.
- The page breaks off while invoking reference [7], p.165, Prop. 2.3. Its identity is not established; it may be Cartan–Eilenberg, but that is unsure. The aim is to conclude that W is projective as a W^e-module, i.e. separable.

The page serves the sheaf-theoretic Brauer group: Azumaya algebras over ringed spaces, and the fact that End of a vector bundle is Azumaya.
errors: The transcription writes μ(f⊗m)(n) = f(n)(m); the intended formula is f(n)·m. This is a typographic/notational quirk, not a mathematical error.
Lemma III.3 is correct: End_A(M) is always separable for M finitely generated projective. It is central (Azumaya) only when M is faithful, but the lemma claims only separability.
The proof is truncated at the page end, so the final step is not visible.

ideas.what: Characterisation of locally Azumaya sheaves of algebras on a ringed space via finite presentation plus central separable stalks
ideas.modern_name: Azumaya algebra over a ringed space / scheme (stalkwise criterion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman (1960) for rings; Grothendieck, 'Le groupe de Brauer I' (1966/68), for ringed spaces and topoi
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas)

ideas.what: End_A(M) is separable for M finitely generated projective, via Hom(M,A)⊗M ≅ End(M) and projectivity over W
ideas.modern_name: Endomorphism algebras of vector bundles are Azumaya (separable)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (as a standard fact)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused sheet from someone else's typescript on Azumaya algebras over ringed spaces. Its content is standard Auslander–Goldman material and is unrelated to Grothendieck's notes on the adjacent pages.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down. It is a typed English text by another author, not Grothendieck's handwriting.
μ(f⊗m)(n) = f(n)(m) should read f(n)m (i.e. f(n)·m).
The handwritten '13' in the corner is the archive page number.
